paper_title: Recent progress of Y-series electron acceptors for organic solar cells
source_file: /home/wzfeng/MySearch/PhotoRag/MD/Nano Select - 2021 - Lu - Recent progress of Y‐series electron acceptors for organic solar cells/auto/Nano Select - 2021 - Lu - Recent progress of Y‐series electron acceptors for organic solar cells.md

knowledge_points.content: Y-series acceptors are characterized by an A-DA'D-A type fused-ring structure, which differs from ITIC-type acceptors by incorporating an electron-deficient aromatic ring into the central core and replacing cyclopentadienyls with pyrrole rings.
knowledge_points.evidence: Relative to IT1C derivatives, the most prominent differences of chemical structures of Y6 are the introduction of electron-deficient aromatic rings into the middle of the central cores and the replacement of the cyclopentadienyls with pyrrole rings... Zou proposed A-DA'D-A type fused-ring electron acceptor design strategy.

knowledge_points.content: Single-junction organic solar cells based on the Y6 acceptor have achieved power conversion efficiencies (PCE) exceeding 18%, with a specific report of 18.22% for the binary D18/Y6 system.
knowledge_points.evidence: Nowadays the PCE of single-junction PSCs devices based on Y6 has achieved exceed 18%... Ding groups obtained 18.22% efficiency for binary OSCs based on D18/Y6.

knowledge_points.content: Replacing the sulfur atom in the central benzothiadiazole (BT) unit with selenium (forming Y6Se) results in a narrower optical bandgap of 1.32 eV and an increased short-circuit current (Jsc) of 27.98 mA cm⁻².
knowledge_points.evidence: Lin chose D18 as donor to blend with Y6Se to obtain higher PCE of 17.7% due to the increase of Jsc... Y6Se [has] Eg of 1.32 eV and Jsc of 27.98 mA cm-2.

knowledge_points.content: The solubility of Y-series acceptors is significantly influenced by the alkyl chains on the nitrogen atoms of the pyrrole rings; while straight-chain N-C11 shows poor solubility, branched chains like those in N3 and N4 enhance solubility.
knowledge_points.evidence: It seems that the alkyl chains connected with nitrogen atoms play a decisive role in solubility of molecules. For example N-C11 with straight alkyl chains on the N atoms showed poor solubility, while the solubility is significantly enhanced form Y6 to N3 to N4.

knowledge_points.content: The length of branched side chains affects molecular packing; in the BTP-4Cl series, the C12 side chain (BTP-4Cl-12) yields the shortest π-π stacking distance and the best device performance compared to C8 or C16 chains.
knowledge_points.evidence: Among these molecules of BTP-4Cl-8, BTP-4Cl-12, and BTP-4Cl-16, BTP-4Cl-12 has the shortest π-π stacking distance, and showed the best performance whether in spin-coated OSCs or in blade-coated OsCs.

knowledge_points.content: Y-series acceptors facilitate efficient charge transport through a 3D network formed by two distinct π-π stacking modes: one between the end groups and another through the interaction of the fused-ring cores (D' units).
knowledge_points.evidence: There are two π-π stacking modes for Y-series acceptor. One is similar with ITIC class NFAs, and another is the π-π stacking through the interaction of the D' units, which construct 3D network that facilitate charge transport.

knowledge_points.content: The introduction of trifluoromethyl (CF3) groups on the end groups of Y-series acceptors, as seen in BTIC-CF3-γ, results in a smaller molecular dihedral angle, which promotes intermolecular charge transfer and leads to a PCE of 15.59%.
knowledge_points.evidence: The new NFA BTIC-CF3–γ exhibited the smallest dihedral angle... which contributes to the intermolecular charge transfer for high Jsc and FF. The devices based on PBDB-TF/BTIC-CF3–γ yielded a PCE of 15.59%.

knowledge_points.content: The Y-series acceptor BTP-e9, featuring optimized side chain lengths on the edge of the core, achieved a high PCE of 17.8% with a high fill factor (FF) of 81.1% when blended with PBDB-TF.
knowledge_points.evidence: BTP-e9 [has] Voc of 0.839 V, Jsc of 26.2 mA cm-2, FF of 81.1%, and PCE of 17.8%.

knowledge_points.content: The success of Y-series acceptors is attributed to reduced non-radiative energy losses, high electroluminescence quantum efficiency, and a sharp absorption tail, all of which contribute to higher open-circuit voltage (Voc).
knowledge_points.evidence: The energy losses especially the nonradiative energy losses were reduced in OSCs based on Y-series acceptors, which is beneficial for the high Voc. Sharp absorption tail and high electroluminescence quantum efficiency are the main factors.

knowledge_points.content: The molecule BZIC, reported in 2017, was a precursor to Y6 that utilized a dithieno[3,2-b]pyrrolobenzotriazole core, though it only achieved a PCE of 6.3% due to low Jsc and FF.
knowledge_points.evidence: Zou pioneered the use of dithieno[3,2-b]pyrrolobenzotriazole as cores to construct a new type NFA BzIc... the devices based on HFQx-T/BZIC only gave a PCE of 6.3% due to the low short-circuit current density (Jsc) and fill factor (FF).

knowledge_points.content: Substitution of the outer thiophene units with thieno[3,2-b]furan (BPF-4F) increases molecular twisting compared to thieno[3,2-b]thiophene (BTP-4F) due to oxygen-oxygen repulsion, affecting charge transfer properties.
knowledge_points.evidence: BPF-4F is even more twisted than BPT-4F and BPS-4F due to the two O atoms that repulse each other... Different O...O, S...O, and Se...O noncovalent interactions endow them with different molecule geometries.

knowledge_points.content: Asymmetric end-group engineering using both Cl and Br atoms (BTP-ClBr) resulted in a PCE of 16.82% and an exceptionally high fill factor (FF) of 79% due to balanced charge mobilities.
knowledge_points.evidence: BTP-ClBr based devices gave the highest PCE of 16.82% with the highest FF of 79% due to the balanced hole and electron mobilities.
